x: Pat Newell, taking over Jack Brown's cloak, proved a worthy successor on the hard grind from Crawley to Handcross, and in gaining two places brought us within sight of all but T.V.H. who had widened their lead,through a grand run by Bert Ingles, to 2½ minutes over the second club, Woodford.
White took Woodford into a lead here which they kept to the end, while Bert Ingles drew away from Alan to increase the Valley's lead over us to 29s.
Charlie Walker, on the eighth stage, was also disappointing with 18.49 and dropped us back to fourth after a battle royal over the last half-mile with Alan Perkins(Ilford) and Bert Ingles (T.V.H.).
